items.title: 52263_Sonny Greer oral history interview
items.q: We had a bass player Bass Edwards, he used to record with us a lot. Played one of them big Sousaphones, this cat played with Charlie Johnson band at Small's Paradise. Charlie Johnson had a good band.

ctx.x: If you didn't make the scene, because all the faces would come down, all the musicians, white ones, all of them, Tommy Dorsey, Jimmy and all of them, the whole crowd. Red Nichols, all of them. Red Nichols played down the corner from us, from the Kentucky Club.

They would come up to Harlem and hang out all the joints, to steal, see what the cats was putting out. They could play what was on paper, but you couldn't tell them go on out there and play me some choruses. We had a bass player Bass Edwards, he used to record with us a lot. Played one of them big Sousaphones, this cat played with Charlie Johnson

band at Small's Paradise. Charlie Johnson had a good band. (Stafford) Georgie, his drummer, Jabo, and all them sharks in there. This this big. And he had a light in the bell. He'd take the tray and fan Bass Edwards, he took a waiter's tray, like the trumpet player play and play you ten choruses like on the trumpet and he always had cigar, never take it out of his mouth.
